checklist.title: Falsify Polynomial Addition Degree Invariant: Can add_polynomialcoeff produce incorrect result degree or fail to zero-pad shorter polynomials?

reachability.notes: Polynomial addition is used extensively in interpolation and recovery. Incorrect addition corrupts all downstream results.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the add_polynomialcoeff function in SG-008 module. 2. Create test cases with polynomials of different degrees: (a) deg(a) > deg(b), (b) deg(a) < deg(b), (c) deg(a) == deg(b). 3. For each case, verify result degree equals max(deg(a), deg(b)). 4. Test edge cases: empty polynomials, single-coefficient polynomials, polynomials with leading zero coefficients. 5. Verify zero-padding: when adding [1,2,3] + [4,5], confirm shorter polynomial is treated as [4,5,0] internally. 6. Check for off-by-one errors in degree calculation. 7. Trace downstream usage in interpolation and recovery functions to verify corrupted addition would propagate errors.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0063, Invariant: SG-008:INV-001. This is an internal invariant governing polynomial arithmetic correctness. Violation would corrupt Shamir secret sharing interpolation and recovery operations.

checklist.title: Falsify Polynomial Multiplication Degree Invariant: Can multiply_polynomialcoeff produce incorrect result degree or convolution errors?

reachability.notes: Polynomial multiplication is used in vanishing polynomial construction and interpolation.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the multiply_polynomialcoeff function in SG-009 module. 2. Verify result degree invariant: for polynomials a (degree m) and b (degree n), result must have degree m+n. 3. Verify convolution correctness: result[k] = sum(a[i] * b[k-i]) for all valid i. 4. Test edge cases: (a) zero-degree polynomials (constants), (b) one polynomial has degree 0, (c) polynomials with zero coefficients in middle positions, (d) maximum degree polynomials near buffer limits. 5. Test with leading zero coefficients to verify degree calculation handles coefficient cancellation. 6. Verify buffer allocation: result buffer must accommodate deg(a) + deg(b) + 1 coefficients. 7. Check for off-by-one errors in loop bounds during convolution. 8. Trace usage in vanishing polynomial construction to verify corrupted multiplication would propagate to proof verification.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0064, Invariant: SG-009:INV-002. Incorrect polynomial multiplication corrupts vanishing polynomial construction and interpolation, potentially causing invalid proofs to be accepted or valid proofs to be rejected.

checklist.title: Falsify Polynomial Division Invariant: Can non-exact division in divide_polynomialcoeff produce incorrect quotients?

reachability.notes: Division is used in compute_kzg_proof_multi_impl. If the division is not exact, the discarded remainder introduces errors.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify all call sites of divide_polynomialcoeff within compute_kzg_proof_multi_impl and related KZG proof generation paths. 2. Construct test cases where polynomial 'a' is NOT exactly divisible by polynomial 'b' (i.e., remainder != 0). 3. Verify that the invariant a = quotient * b + remainder holds by computing quotient * b + remainder and comparing to original 'a'. 4. Check if there are any code paths that call divide_polynomialcoeff with inputs that could produce non-zero remainders. 5. If non-exact division occurs, verify the impact on downstream KZG proof correctness by checking if corrupted quotients lead to invalid proofs that could be accepted or valid proofs that could be rejected.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0065, Invariant: SG-010:INV-002. Property Type: invariant. Primary Element: SG-010:divide_polynomialcoeff. The discarded remainder is only correct when division is exact - any non-exact division path represents a potential correctness violation affecting KZG proof integrity.

checklist.title: Falsify Lagrange Interpolation Correctness: Can interpolate_polynomialcoeff produce a polynomial with incorrect degree or fail to satisfy evaluation constraints?

reachability.notes: Interpolation is used in the batch verification equation. Incorrect interpolation causes the verification to produce wrong results.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the interpolate_polynomialcoeff function in SG-011 module. 2. Verify the post-condition: result polynomial degree MUST be at most len(xs) - 1. 3. Verify interpolation correctness: for all i, evaluate(result, xs[i]) MUST equal ys[i]. 4. Test Lagrange basis polynomial construction: verify each L_i(x) satisfies L_i(xs[j]) = 1 if i==j else 0. 5. Test edge cases: (a) single point interpolation (degree 0 constant), (b) two points (degree 1 line), (c) maximum supported number of points. 6. Test with duplicate x-values: function should either reject or handle gracefully (undefined behavior for Lagrange interpolation). 7. Test with zero x-values and zero y-values to check for division-by-zero or special case handling. 8. Verify finite field arithmetic precision: check that intermediate Lagrange basis calculations do not overflow or lose precision. 9. Trace downstream usage in batch verification equation to confirm corrupted interpolation would cause valid proofs to be rejected or invalid proofs to be accepted.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0066, Invariant: SG-011:INV-003. Property Type: post-condition. Primary Element: SG-011:interpolate_polynomialcoeff. The Lagrange interpolation correctness property is critical for batch verification - incorrect interpolation could cause valid proofs to be rejected (availability impact) or invalid proofs to be accepted (integrity impact).
